newsitem.title: USA: CIA chief Deutch made hush-hush visit to China.
newsitem.headline: CIA chief Deutch made hush-hush visit to China.

text.p: CIA Director John Deutch visited China last week on a previously unannounced stop during an Asian tour and discussed threats to international security, the Central Intelligence Agency said on Monday.

Deutch "met a number of Chinese government officials to exchange views on a range of important global trends and concerns and to discuss transnational threats to the security of all nations," a CIA spokesman said.

Deutch visited China October 14 to 16 before flying to South Korea with Winston Lord, the assistant secretary of state for East Asian and Pacific affairs, on a previously reported trip, spokesman Mark Mansfield said.
The CIA refused to name Chinese officials with whom Deutch met. It also declined to discuss his current whereabouts, but said he left South Korea on Sunday and was visiting another Asian country.

Deutch's China trip followed reports that Beijing had sold a new batch of nuclear weapons-related equipment to Pakistan in an alleged deal that could boost pressure on President Bill Clinton to impose economic sanctions.

The Washington Times reported October 9 that Beijing secretly sold Islamabad last month a special industrial furnace and diagnostic equipment with military applications that could be used in Pakistan's nuclear facilities, which are not subject to international inspection.
Quoting what it said was a top-secret CIA memorandum dated September 14, the article said the State Department had protested to China about the matter on August 30.

At the time, the U.S. State Department denied that China had breached a promise to the United States by selling nuclear weapons-related equipment to Pakistan, but stopped short of denying the reported transfer had occurred.
